newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's car union workers protest Samsung report.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's car union workers protest Samsung report.

text.p: About 500 union workers from South Korea's car industry on Friday demanded that the Samsung Group drop its auto enterprise to avoid excess capacity in the industry, witnesses said.

Demonstrators briefly scuffled with police outside the Samsung Group headquarters. The workers had sought a personal meeting with Samsung chairman Lee Kun-hee to ask him to withdraw from the crowded industry.

"Samsung's alleged takeover attempts are disrupting the nation's car industry," said a statement distributed by car union workers, who were mainly from Kia Motors, considered Samsung's most attractive takeover target.
"If Samsung really thinks about the nation's economy, it should drop its car venture and focus more on fostering its main semiconductor industry," the statement said.

Analysts said Samsung was measuring public opinion about a possible takeover when it proposed in an internal report, which was widely believed to have been intentionally leaked to the press, to restructure the crowded domestic auto industry.
An industry shake-out would benefit a company with Samsung's deep pockets. But the report set off a firestorm of criticism.
